main_body: Timber-framed house with a tiled hip roof, a front gable dormer, a chimney, plaster walls with beams and two wooden doors
top_band: Roof tile slopes, orange/red with light highlight tiles, rows ~0-42 across the roof. At x=107 the dark-edged tile rows run 4-43. A dark eave row (L=15) sits at rows 44-45, then the wall starts.
evidence: The big sloped roof planes are seen from above and read as the top surface. They end at a dark eave line, with a shaded band under it. Below sit the plaster and timber front walls with the doors and window set between beams. The structure matches the Beodeul house references, so it counts as a correct 3/4 building. The side roof hips and the gable dormer slope are not drawn as receding isometric side faces.

style.evidence: The measured facts match or beat the references: 18 colours per tile (the same as house-h101_0), 0% flat fill and 202 distinct colours. Only 12% of dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outlines are tinted dark brown and red-brown. The roof tiles have per-tile highlights and several tone steps, and the plaster has speckle. The beams are shaded, and the door has studs and a handle. It would sit comfortably next to the references.
